---
title: "Memory Measurement Model, simple span"
subtitle: "Categorical recall: a correct item, other list items and new lures compete for the response"
model: m3
---

## What the model says

The memory measurement model (M3), implemented in the R package bmm, treats recall as a choice among
response candidates: the options a participant can give. Candidates that receive activation from the
same sources form a category. In a simple-span task, a list is studied and one serial position is
cued, which gives three categories, labelled as in bmm: the item at the cued position (`corr`), the
other items of the list (`other`), and candidates that were not on the list (`npl`, not-presented
lures). The activation of each category is a sum of parameters:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{corr} &= b + a + c \\
\text{other} &= b + a \\
\text{npl} &= b
\end{aligned}
$$

Here `b` is background activation, `a` general activation and `c` context activation (all three
explained below). A choice rule turns the activations $A_i$ into the probability $p_i$ of a response
from category $i$, with each category weighted by its number of candidates $n_i$ (`num_options` in
bmm). The sums run over the three categories:

$$
\text{simple:}\quad p_i = \frac{n_i A_i}{\sum_j n_j A_j}
\qquad\qquad
\text{softmax:}\quad p_i = \frac{n_i e^{A_i}}{\sum_j n_j e^{A_j}}
$$

The background activation `b` is shared by every candidate. One parameter has to be fixed to set the
scale, and bmm fixes `b`: 0.1 under the simple rule, 0 under softmax. `a` and `c` are therefore read
relative to `b`. `a` is general activation: every item on
the current list receives it, so it lifts the cued item and the other list items above the lures.
`c` is context activation: it comes from the cue and goes only to the item at the cued position, so
it separates the correct response from the other list items.

## The task

```{=html}
<div class="ex-task">
  <svg id="m3-task" role="img" aria-label="A studied list of letters, the cue for one position, and the response screen with the candidates"></svg>
  <div class="ex-legend" id="m3-task-legend"></div>
</div>
```

One trial is cued recall from a candidate set. A list of letters is studied, a serial position is
cued, and the participant picks the letter from that position among the candidates on the screen.
The candidates are the correct letter (blue), the other letters of the list (orange) and letters
that were not on the list (grey). N is the number of candidates, 1 + `n_other` + `n_npl`; the drawing
follows these two counts as they are set in the controls below.

```{=html}
    <input type="range" id="m3-n-npl" min="0" max="12" step="1">
    <input type="number" id="m3-n-npl-num" min="0" max="12" step="1" aria-label="n_npl">
    <div class="ex-hint" id="m3-range-hint"></div>

  <svg id="m3-bars" role="img" aria-label="Predicted probability of a correct response, an other-list-item response and a lure response"></svg>
  <div class="ex-legend">
    Filled bars: current values. Dashed outlines: a = 1, c = 2 with the same counts and rule.
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="m3-reset">Reset</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

Every change redraws the bars, the drawing above and the plot below. The bars are the probabilities
of the three response categories, summed over the candidates in each, so they add up to 1. The dashed
outlines stay at the starting values `a` = 1, `c` = 2; Reset returns all four controls to the start.
Raising `a` moves responses from the lures to the list; raising `c` moves them from the other list
items to the correct one. Switching the rule keeps the numbers but changes their meaning: under the
simple rule activations are ratios to `b`, under softmax only differences between activations count.
The counts change the bars as well, with `a` and `c` held fixed; the next section follows that up.

## Across task settings

```{=html}
<div class="ex-widget">
  <svg id="m3-across" role="img" aria-label="Predicted probability correct against response-set size for three ways of adding candidates"></svg>
  <div class="ex-legend">
    Candidates added as <span class="grey">lures</span>, as <span class="orange">other list items</span>,
    or as <span class="purple">both in equal numbers</span>. Solid: simple rule. Dashed: softmax.
    Circle: the current settings.
  </div>
  <p class="ex-legend" id="m3-across-now"></p>
</div>
```

The counts $n_i$ enter the probabilities $p_i$, and through them the likelihood (the probability the
model assigns to the observed responses). The model therefore predicts how recall changes with the size
of the response set without a new parameter: `a` and `c` stay as set above, and only the number of
candidates in each category changes. Every added candidate adds to the denominator of the choice rule,
so P(correct) falls as N grows. How fast it falls depends on what is added. Other list items have
activation `b + a`, so for positive `a` they compete harder than lures, which have only `b`. Softmax allows negative values; the simple rule needs `b + a` and
`b + a + c` to stay at or above 0 with `b` = 0.1, so its lines disappear when `a` or `a + c` goes below
−0.1.

## In bmm

```{=html}
<div class="ex-widget">
  <pre class="ex-code" id="m3-code"></pre>
  <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" id="m3-copy">Copy</button>
</div>
<script type="module" src="../js/pages/m3.js"></script>
```

The code updates with the controls. `m3()` defines the model (`version = "ss"` is the simple-span
version), `dm3()` returns the log probability of a set of response counts, and `bmf()` writes the
formula for `bmm()`, which fits `a` and `c` to data. `b` is not passed: bmm adds it from the choice
rule. See the
[M3 article](https://venpopov.com/bmm/articles/bmm_m3.html) for the full model, including the
complex-span version and custom activation functions, and the reference pages for
[`m3()`](https://venpopov.com/bmm/reference/m3.html) and
[`dm3()`](https://venpopov.com/bmm/reference/m3dist.html).
